```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive lx-cards" data-learn="a01" data-src="../assets/learn/data/07-cost.json ../assets/learn/data/a01-project-tea.json ../assets/learn/data/path.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">A 150 MW wind farm in seven moves (real 2025 dollars)</p>
<ol>
<li>Year 0 spends $256.8M on building the farm. Years 1 to 30 each sell $22.2M of power at $50/MWh and spend $5.2M on upkeep: $17.0M net.</li>
<li>Discounted at 4% a year, the 30 net years are worth $294.3M today, so the net present value (NPV) is +$37.5M.</li>
<li>The discount rate is what the money costs. With loans at 5% and owners at 10% (nominal, both held fixed), 60% loans give 4.39% real and an NPV of +$24.1M; 40% loans give −$5.7M.</li>
<li>The NPV reaches zero at 5.17%, the internal rate of return (IRR).</li>
<li>The cash put in is back in year 16 (year 24 discounted). With a 20-year life, payback is still year 16, but the NPV is −$25.5M.</li>
<li>The NPV crosses zero at a price of $45.11/MWh, lesson 7's levelized cost of the same farm.</li>
<li>Swung across its range, the capacity factor moves the NPV most ($204.5M), then the discount rate ($170.0M) and the price ($153.6M).</li>
</ol>
<div class="a1-tables">

<li>Building cost $1,712 per <span class="lx-term" data-term="kilowatt">kW</span> and fixed upkeep $34.57 per kW a year: <a href="https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/aeo/assumptions/pdf/EMM_Assumptions.pdf">EIA, AEO2026 assumptions, Table 3</a> (2025 dollars, April 2026).</li>
```

## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="a1-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Cash flow</dt><dd>Money in minus money out, year by year: the outlay in year 0, then sales minus upkeep.</dd>
<dt>Net present value</dt><dd>Every year's cash discounted to today and added up, the outlay included: +$37.5M for the farm at 4%.</dd>
<dt>WACC</dt><dd>The blended rate the project pays lenders and owners: its discount rate.</dd>
<dt>Internal rate of return</dt><dd>The rate at which the NPV is exactly zero: 5.17% for the farm.</dd>
<dt>Payback</dt><dd>The first year in which the running sum of cash reaches zero: year 16, or year 24 discounted. It ignores every year after.</dd>
<dt>Break-even price</dt><dd>The price that gives an NPV of zero: $45.11/MWh, the farm's LCOE.</dd>
</dl>
<div class="a1-tables">
<!-- a1-yard:start (written by _tests/learn/test_a01-project-tea.js --write; do not edit) -->
<table class="a1-static" aria-label="Four yardsticks for the same farm">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Yardstick</th><th scope="col">This farm</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td>Net present value at 4%</td><td>+$37.5M</td></tr>
<tr><td>Internal rate of return</td><td>5.17%</td></tr>
<tr><td>Simple payback</td><td>year 16</td></tr>
<tr><td>Discounted payback at 4%</td><td>year 24</td></tr>
<tr><td>Break-even price</td><td>$45.11/MWh</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
<!-- a1-yard:end -->
</div>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>What these cash flows leave out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Taxes and credits.** A real project pays income tax and may earn tax credits; depreciation lowers the tax. They change the cash every year, which is why agencies' numbers differ from these.
- **The money's mix.** Step 3 held both rates fixed. More loans make the owners' share riskier, so owners ask more: the real WACC may fall less than the slider shows, or not at all.
- **Loan size.** Lenders cap a loan by the cash that must repay it, so the loan share is not free to choose.
- **Two views of one project.** These are the project's cash flows before loan payments, discounted at the WACC. Owners also judge their own cash after loan payments, at their own rate: the owners' IRR.
- **Where it stops.** Loan sizing and capital structure stay at awareness level in this course (side shelf [X5](x05-project-finance.html)). No investment advice.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Nominal cash flows, spreadsheets and models</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Real or nominal, never mixed.** Here prices stay in 2025 dollars and the rate is real. A nominal analysis inflates each year's cash and uses a nominal rate, $(1 + \text{nominal}) = (1 + \text{real})(1 + \text{inflation})$ (K3): the same NPV.
- **A flat contract price.** The $50/MWh here is fixed in 2025 dollars, as a contract indexed to inflation would be. A price flat in nominal dollars buys less each year, so its real revenue falls.
- **Spreadsheets.** A spreadsheet's NPV function counts its first value as year 1, so add the year-0 outlay outside it: NPV(4%, years 1 to 30) − 256.8. IRR takes all 31 years, year 0 included.
- **Inside a model.** A planning model charges each MW a yearly cost instead (K3, lesson 13): with these inputs, 1 MW of wind costs \$133,575 a year, and $133{,}575 \div (0.338 \times 8{,}760) = 45.11$ \$/MWh, the break-even price.
- **Where it goes.** Modeler lesson [M11](m11-tea-in-models.html) puts a project's cash flow inside the optimization.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="a1-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="irr" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Of two projects, the one with the higher IRR is the better one to build.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth, when only one can be built. A 20 MW farm at a 43% capacity factor returns 8.12% but adds $18.9M; the 150 MW farm returns 5.17% and adds $37.5M. NPV counts the size.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="payback" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A project that pays back early enough is worth building.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. With a 20-year life the farm still pays back in year 16, yet its NPV is −$25.5M: payback ignores the time value of money and every year after it.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="yearly" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A positive NPV means the project makes money every year.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Year 0 is −$256.8M. The NPV is one sum of all years at today's value, +$37.5M at 4%.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="above" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If a project's IRR is above its discount rate, its NPV is positive.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact, for cash like this farm's: one outlay, then only positive years, so the NPV falls as the rate rises. Projects with later outlays can have several IRRs, or none.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="a1">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="seven" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">The money costs 7% real instead of 4%. Is the farm still worth building at $50/MWh?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">Yes: its NPV is +$37.5M</li><li data-value="b">No: its NPV is −$45.6M</li><li data-value="c">Yes: it still pays back in year 16</li><li data-value="d">It cannot be told without taxes</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>No: at 7% the NPV is −$45.6M, because 7% is above the farm's 5.17% IRR. +$37.5M is the NPV at 4%; simple payback does not depend on the rate.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="spb" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">The farm costs $256.8M and nets $17.0M a year. In years, how long until its cash is back, not discounted?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">8.56 years</li><li data-value="b">12.00 years</li><li data-value="c">15.09 years</li><li data-value="d">30.00 years</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>15.09 years: 256.8 ÷ 17.02 = 15.09, so the running sum first reaches zero in year 16.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="a1-drill"></div>
<div class="lx-card a1-task">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Build it yourself · about 20 minutes</p>
<p>Rebuild the farm in a spreadsheet (toolbox <a href="k07-spreadsheets.html">K7</a>) and check this page.</p>
<ol>
<li>Row 1 holds the headers: <code>Year</code> in A1 and <code>Cash ($M)</code> in B1. Years 0 to 30 go in A2 to A32.</li>
<li>Cash: −256.8 in B2 (year 0), then 22.2066 − 5.1855 in B3 to B32 (years 1 to 30).</li>
<li>NPV: <code>=NPV(4%, B3:B32) + B2</code> gives 37.53. IRR: <code>=IRR(B2:B32)</code> gives 5.17%.</li>
<li>Change the price to $45.11 (sales 20.0348): the NPV should be about zero. Then try a 20-year life.</li>
</ol>
</div>
```
